label: SYNTHETIC READERS: a test instrument, never readers. Not a choice: the editor chooses (book.json Q3).

candidates.N1: Agentic Workflows, Shown Working: how a team of agents built a talk in a day, and how to build yours
candidates.N2: The Agentic Team: a walkthrough of agentic workflows, from an empty repository to a talk on stage
candidates.N7: Agents That Work Together: a guided tour of agentic workflows, and how to build yours
candidates.N8: Brakes So We Can Go Faster: a guided tour of an agentic team at work, and how to build yours

method: title and subtitle alone; which would you pick up, which would you buy, why; and for N8, whether its subtitle answers the journalist's warning

personas.why: It still opens with a word my committee uses, and now it promises a tour, not a lecture.
personas.second: Second: none; the other three start with 'agents' or 'agentic'.

personas.why: Brakes are the controls; 'an agentic team at work' tells me it is a real team, not a thought experiment.
'Shown working' is still the strongest claim of proof; N8 is catchier but I buy evidence.
personas.second: Second: N8, now that it carries 'how to build yours'.

personas.why: Plain words, and 'work together' is the hard part; but 'a guided tour' is softer than N3's protocols, provenance and memory.
personas.second: Second: N1. Would still rather have N3's subtitle.

personas.why: The hook survives and the subtitle is now one breath; best cover of the four.
personas.second: Second: N2, still the cleanest type.

personas.why: 'Work together' is my job, and 'how to build yours' means my team could run it.
Still the headline. On my warning: the subtitle grounds it in a real team, but does not qualify the claim; the title still says the brakes made the speed.
personas.second: Second: N1, for 'built a talk in a day'.

personas.why: The hook and the promise in one title: I would pick it up and I would know what I get.
